result:
**I'd make curiosity, evidence, and long-term thinking the default human operating system instead of tribal loyalty, short-term status, and motivated reasoning.**

Most large-scale problems—poverty traps, preventable disease, resource conflicts, environmental damage, bad policy, and even many interpersonal cruelties—stem from people (and institutions) systematically undervaluing truth and future consequences relative to immediate group affiliation or personal comfort. Fix the incentive and cognitive defaults and a huge fraction of coordination failures become solvable without needing a dictator, a new ideology, or magical technology.

This isn't "make everyone nicer." Niceness without accuracy just produces well-intentioned disasters. It's closer to raising the sanity waterline: better Bayesian updating, lower time-preference, and treating "I might be wrong" as a feature rather than a social threat. Scientific and technological progress would accelerate because fewer resources would be wasted on signaling, denial, and rent-seeking. Coordination would improve because shared maps of reality beat competing sacred narratives.

Trade-offs exist (some beautiful local cultures and high-variance personalities would be flattened), and implementation would be the hard part—culture and institutions are stubborn. But if I get only one lever, that's the highest-leverage one: change what people actually optimize for when no one is watching. Everything else (energy abundance, better medicine, space settlement, etc.) becomes far easier afterward.

The universe is already stranger and more interesting than our current stories about it. We'd just start noticing.

message.reasoning:
The question is: "If you could change the world in one way, what would it be?"
I'd make curiosity the default setting for every human mind. Not just a hobby, but the default operating system—everyone wakes up thinking "what's actually true here?" instead of "what's the tribe saying?" or "what feels good?"

One generation of that shift and most of the world's problems solve themselves: science accelerates 100x, people stop falling for obvious nonsense, leaders get held accountable, conflicts shrink because everyone starts asking the same questions. The rest of the world (AI, fusion, Mars, whatever) becomes solvable because the bottleneck was never resources or technology—it was always human rationality.

Everything else is just downstream of that. I'd 100% rather live in a world where people are a little less tribal and a lot more truth-seeking than one where we magically end poverty or war without fixing the wiring. Curiosity is the cheat code. Everything else follows. 

What about you? What's the one change you'd make? I'm curious.
